headline: GOLD leaders say COPD's old narrative is outdated in 2027 update
dek: The American Journal of Managed Care reports that leaders of GOLD describe the traditional narrative around COPD as outdated, in connection with a 2027 update.
body:
GOLD leaders say the old narrative around chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is outdated, according to a news item published by The American Journal of Managed Care.

The item links the statement to a 2027 update. The text available for this article consists only of the headline and publisher name, and it does not identify the individual GOLD leaders, describe what the old narrative was, or set out what the update contains.

Further detail was not available in the source material.
key_quote: COPD’s Old Narrative Is Outdated, GOLD Leaders Say in 2027 Update

source.title: COPD’s Old Narrative Is Outdated, GOLD Leaders Say in 2027 Update - The American Journal of Managed Care
source.author_name: The American Journal of Managed Care

headline: Vaccine Guidance Review Panel endorses influenza, RSV and COVID-19 recommendations
dek: The American Thoracic Society said on X that the multi-medical society panel endorsed recommendations on influenza, RSV and COVID-19 vaccines for adults and children.
body:
The Vaccine Guidance Review Panel has announced its endorsement of influenza, RSV and COVID-19 recommendations for adults and children, according to a post from the American Thoracic Society (ATS).

The ATS described the panel as "a multi-medical society effort". In the post, published on X on 5 November 2026, the society directed readers to a linked page to learn more.

The post did not set out the content of the recommendations, name the participating societies or explain how the panel reached its decision. Readers seeking those details are referred to the material linked from the post.

The ATS's profile on X describes it as a leading medical association dedicated to advancing pulmonary, critical care and sleep medicine globally, with more than 22,000 members.
key_quote: announced its endorsement of influenza, RSV and COVID-19 recommendations for adults and children

issues: The article says the ATS's "profile on X" describes it as a leading medical association with more than 22,000 members. The source only supplies this as author_bio metadata and does not say it comes from the X profile, so the attribution to the profile is unsupported.

headline: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis markedly affects quality of life, but no disease-specific monitoring tool exists
dek: ERS publications said on X that existing tools for monitoring health-related quality of life in chronic pulmonary aspergillosis lack specificity or validity, highlighting the need for a CPA-specific measure.
body:
Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) has a profound effect on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), according to a summary posted by ERS publications on X.

The post states that the tools currently available for monitoring HRQoL in the condition have shortcomings. According to the summary, existing instruments lack disease specificity, are complex, or have limited validity.

On that basis, the summary highlights the need for an HRQoL tool designed specifically for CPA. The post does not describe how such a tool might be developed or what it would contain.

ERS publications posted the summary on 7 November 2026, with links to further material. The post itself does not give details of the study design, participants or results, and it does not name the authors or the specific journal.
key_quote: existing monitoring tools lack disease specificity, are complex or have limited validity

issues: The headline says "no disease-specific monitoring tool exists", which the source does not state. The post says existing tools "lack disease specificity, are complex or have limited validity". The "or" implies some tools may be disease-specific but complex or of limited validity. The need for a CPA-specific tool does not establish that none exists, so the headline overstates the source.

headline: Nurse-led protocolled asthma care improved control in children in primary care
dek: A study in ERJ Open Research reports better asthma control in children receiving protocolled, nurse-led care in primary care, according to ERS publications.
body:
Protocolled, nurse-led asthma care improved asthma control in children treated in primary care, according to a study published in ERJ Open Research and highlighted in a post on X by ERS publications.

The post described the work as the first study to assess nurse-led asthma care in children in primary care. It said that protocolled care "significantly improved asthma control using validated measures and spirometry."

According to the post, the small number of visits required makes implementation feasible. The post did not state how many children took part, their ages, the size of the improvement or how long they were followed.

ERS publications lists its titles as the European Respiratory Journal, European Respiratory Review, ERJ Open Research, Breathe, the ERS Monograph and ERS Handbooks, and the European Lung White Book. The post includes links, but this report is based only on the text of the post.
key_quote: Protocolled care significantly improved asthma control using validated measures and spirometry.

issues: The tag "trial" is not supported by the source. The post only says "study" and gives no design, so labelling it a trial asserts a study design the source does not state. The body text itself is accurate and the quote is verbatim.

headline: Ivonescimab achieves 50.7% pCR rate in phase II perioperative NSCLC study
dek: The Clinical Trial Vanguard reports a 50.7% pCR rate for ivonescimab in a phase II study in perioperative non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
body:
Ivonescimab achieved a pathological complete response (pCR) rate of 50.7% in a phase II study in perioperative non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), according to a news item published by The Clinical Trial Vanguard on 6 November 2026.

The item's headline is the only information available from the source. It describes the study as phase II and perioperative, and gives the pCR rate as 50.7%.

The source text does not name the study sponsor, investigators or trial site. It also gives no patient numbers, no treatment regimen, no comparator, no safety findings and no follow-up data. It does not say whether the results have been peer reviewed or presented at a scientific meeting.

Although this item is filed under approvals, the source does not report any regulatory decision for ivonescimab.

Further detail would be needed to place the 50.7% figure in context.
key_quote: Ivonescimab Achieves 50.7% pCR Rate in Phase II Perioperative NSCLC Study

issues: The article says the item is "filed under approvals", but nothing in the source or its metadata mentions an approvals category. This is an unsupported claim, and it also raises a regulatory-decision angle the source never touches.

source.title: Ivonescimab Achieves 50.7% pCR Rate in Phase II Perioperative NSCLC Study - The Clinical Trial Vanguard

headline: Jarushka Naidoo: thanks Irish media for explaining how lung cancer screening saves lives
dek: The thoracic oncologist thanked outlets and Con Shanahan for an explanation of screening's benefit through stage shift, and noted it came to Ireland in a clinical trial.
body:
Jarushka Naidoo, Professor of Medical Oncology at the Cancer Centre Ireland, wrote on X on 10 November 2026 to thank Irish media for their coverage of lung cancer screening.

Naidoo thanked The Irish Times, RTÉ and RTÉ's Drivetime programme. She also thanked Con Shanahan for what she called a "superb explanation of why lung cancer screening saves lives- through stage shift". She did not elaborate on the point in her post.

Naidoo added that screening "came to" Ireland in a clinical trial. The post did not give details of the trial.

She tagged the Irish Cancer Society, the Cancer Centre Ireland and the EU4Health programme, and used the #LCSM hashtag. The post also contained links, but the content they point to was not included in the text of the post.

Naidoo's X profile describes her as a thoracic oncologist with interests in immunotherapy and immune toxicity, and as adjunct faculty at Johns Hopkins University.
key_quote: superb explanation of why lung cancer screening saves lives

issues: The article gives her affiliation as "Cancer Centre Ireland" and says she tagged "the Cancer Centre Ireland". The source only has the handle @CancerCentreIre, so the institution's full name is inferred from a handle and is not supported by the source.
It says she "tagged" the EU4Health programme, but in the source #EU4Health is a hashtag, not a tag. This is minor.
The source does not say who or what "came to" Ireland in a clinical trial. The article asserts that screening did, which is an inference.

headline: Nasal mRNA therapeutic shows numerical symptom reductions in asthma after rhinovirus challenge
dek: Topline data from Ethris show numerical reductions in respiratory symptoms versus placebo in adults with asthma on stable maintenance therapy, according to Healio Allergy and Asthma.
body:
Topline data from Ethris indicate numerical reductions in respiratory symptoms with a nasally delivered mRNA therapeutic compared with placebo in adults with asthma, according to a post by Healio Allergy and Asthma on X.

The reductions were seen after a rhinovirus challenge, the post said. The participants were adults with asthma who were on stable maintenance therapy.

The post described the findings as numerical reductions. It did not give figures, the size of the study, the name of the product or any statistical results, and it provided no further detail on study design or safety. It also did not mention any regulatory decision. The data were described as topline, and the post linked to a report from the account @HealioPulm.

The information in this article is limited to what was stated in the post.
key_quote: a nasally delivered #mRNA therapeutic vs. placebo in adults with #asthma on stable maintenance therapy

issues: The article says the post "linked to a report from the account @HealioPulm." The source only tags @HealioPulm and includes a shortened t.co link. It does not say where the link leads or that it is a report from that account, so the claim is unsupported.

headline: Trial finds insufficient evidence that asthma at-risk registers cut crisis events in primary care
dek: A trial conclusion shared on X says at-risk registers for asthma in primary care were not shown to reduce crisis events, though some indication of benefit was seen.
body:
A trial of at-risk registers for asthma in primary care did not provide sufficient evidence that they reduce asthma-related crisis events, according to a conclusion shared on X.

The post quotes the trial's conclusion: "This trial did not provide sufficient evidence to show that the establishment and integration of at-risk registers for asthma in primary care reduces asthma-related crisis events for people with at-risk asthma, but there was some indication of benefit."

The post was published by an account whose bio describes its owner as a thoracic medicine and asthma physician. It contains the quoted conclusion and a link to the full publication.

The post does not name the journal or the authors. It also gives no details of the trial's size, setting, duration or numerical results, so the extent of the "indication of benefit" cannot be assessed from the post alone.
key_quote: at-risk registers for asthma in primary care reduces asthma-related crisis events for people with at-risk asthma, but there was some indication of benefit

issues: The article says the post contains "a link to the full publication". The source only contains an unlabelled t.co shortlink, so what it points to (full publication, abstract, or something else) is not supported. It should say only that the post includes a link.

The item available to LungDaily consists only of the headline. It does not give the trial name, the number of participants, the size of any difference between treatment arms, safety findings or the setting in which the results were presented.

The report is also not about a regulatory decision. No approval, label change or submission is mentioned in the source text.

Further detail on the design and results will need to come from the full CancerNetwork article or the underlying study report, which were not part of the source material.

headline: Abhishek Tandon: Polluted air weakens lung defences and raises pneumonia risk

body:

Tandon wrote that polluted air compromises lung defences, increasing susceptibility to pneumonia. He added that in people who are already infected, air pollution can worsen inflammation and increase disease severity.

The post included a link to the interview.

headline: Pulmonary Fibrosis Trust to hold first Westminster Briefing, hosted by Jim Shannon MP
dek: The charity said it will present findings from its patient and carer survey at an event in Parliament, hosted by Jim Shannon MP.
body:
The Pulmonary Fibrosis Trust (PF Trust) said it will hold its first ever Westminster Briefing in Parliament on 11 November 2026.

In a post on X on 10 November, the charity said the event will be hosted by Jim Shannon MP. It said it will share findings from its patient and carer survey at the briefing.

According to the post, the aim is to ensure that the voices of people affected by pulmonary fibrosis are heard. The post tagged the House of Commons Health and Social Care Committee account (@CommonsHealth) and used the hashtags #PulmonaryFibrosis and #HiddenInPlainSight.

The post did not give further details of the survey findings, the venue or the programme for the briefing.
key_quote: we'll be sharing findings from our patient & carer survey ensuring the voices of people affected by pulmonary fibrosis are heard.

issues: key_quote is not verbatim from source

The article identifies @CommonsHealth as the 'House of Commons Health and Social Care Committee account'. The source only shows the handle '@CommonsHealth' and never names the committee, so this identification is not supported by the source.
